source_context_corrections.correction: Anchor API semantics to the installed header specification version. The report identifies Level Zero loader 1.32.0 and headers/spec v1.17.24; its 1.16.24/1.19.12 links are API references, not proof of the installed driver build. The official 1.32.0 release pins its headers to spec v1.17.24, whose Sysman page confirms the cited PCI and memory APIs and field semantics. No device result follows.

Retain the memory-counter unit contradiction as unresolved. The official v1.17.24 spec labels readCounter/writeCounter as total bytes, while the same struct says a counter is a 32-byte transaction count and multiplies deltas by 32, with rollover at 2^32. The 128 GiB wrap interval is a derivation, not measured behavior; do not encode a conversion or assume at-most-one wrap until exact driver behavior and valid bits are qualified.
source_context_corrections.evidence: Official v1.17.24 Sysman API zes_mem_bandwidth_t and zes_mem_bandwidth_counter_bits_exp_properties_t.validBitsCount: https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/1.17.24/sysman/api.html

source_context_corrections.correction: Keep Xe GT stats source support separate from host support. The cited /next documentation describes aggregate per-GT debugfs SVM migration/copy counts and times, requires CONFIG_DEBUG_FS, and warns about resetting during active work. It does not establish that the installed kernel exposes the interface or that the counters cover ordinary copy commands, all PCIe traffic, or VRAM bandwidth.

Treat the host root-port/system PMU mention as a generic possible class, not an identified counter on this PC; no platform PMU source is named. XPU-SMI 2.0 documents device/tile telemetry and Arc Pro support; XPUM materials also describe Data Center products. Neither proves consumer Arc B570 support. The report correctly stops short of a B570 support claim.
